answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, an adversary who spins up 172 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 27 times the capital for one share. The sparrow report shows the merge explicitly at each vault. The fee repeats 12 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
